source_context.article: Fox et al. 2017 Nature Ecology & Evolution
source_context.prior_art: deliberate catastrophic local extinction can disrupt spatial synchrony and increase persistence in cycling lab protist metapopulations; phenomenon spatial hydra effect already published

source_context.article: Matter and Roland 2009/2010 Proceedings Royal Society B
source_context.prior_art: severe annual adult removal of 2 of 17 butterfly meadow populations reduced immigration to neighboring meadows, increased local synchrony
reductions in within-generation abundance but limited documented effects on surrounding population persistence

source_context.article: Park et al. 2024 Royal Society Open Science
source_context.prior_art: same butterfly adult-removal experiment, target populations persisted despite 8 generations of observed adult removal, genetic evidence consistent with immigrants from multiple sources; NOT realized local extinction

predeclared_binary_viability_space.state_bits: x=(x1,x2,x3,x4), xi=1 if natal donor potentially viable, 0 if unavailable
predeclared_binary_viability_space.full_global_live_donor_count_histogram: binomial 4 choose k divided by 16 for k=0..4, equal between worlds
proof_obligations: Both 16-state laws nonnegative, exactly total mass 1
Each of six donor pairs has identical joint viability 1/4, covariance 0
Every global source-count state k=0..4 has identical probability, not only matching mean
Both receivers have 3 potentially accessible donors and one excluded donor
Recipient A has donor set {1,2,3}, B has donor set {1,2,4}, both fixed across worlds
A's source-unavailable-all risk and B's must interchange between two worlds
Absolute A risk difference exactly 1/8 and ratio of high/low exactly 3
Aggregate mean risk of A/B equal between worlds; risk redistribution rather than universal improvement

exact_target.outcome: all accessible donor viability bits 0 at source-state observation; NOT measured arrival or local extinction
exact_target.rescue_opportunity_not_actual_rescue: At least one accessible viable donor; potential opportunity only, no arrival/colonization/fitness

required_result.assumption_qualifier: No directed movement intensities, distance or weather given

ecological_question: Even after observing the full global donor-count distribution and every marginal/pairwise donor cofailure relation, does higher-order joint donor unavailability interacting with recipient-specific accessibility predict failure of all local replacement source options?

specific_future_measurement.independent_prospective_study: Four-or-more natal donor groups with independently measured time-resolved viability, source-to-recipient directional access, contemporaneous environmental covariates, and recipient next-interval actual recolonization
specific_future_measurement.primary_mechanism: A recipient-specific triple-donor cutoff/last viable source failure event must predict later true local colonization opportunity or persistence beyond donor count and pairwise synchrony reference.
specific_future_measurement.reference_controls: Number and identities of accessible source islands, empirical marginals and pairwise cofailure, full global donor-count histogram, source-to-recipient distances, habitat/environment/effort, actual source abundance as measured
specific_future_measurement.evidence_boundary: Known truth alone counts ZERO ecological observations, effect sizes, confirmatory runs or evidence of real extinction.
